bio: An Ansari companion of the Khazraj, allied with Banu Bayada and hence called al-Bayadi. He is known for the famous zihar case: he declared zihar from his wife for Ramadan, broke it mid-month, and the Prophet prescribed the graduated expiation, ultimately giving him grain to feed sixty poor people. His hadith was transmitted by Ibn al-Musayyib, Abu Salama, and Sulayman bin Yasar.

bio: An Ansari companion, kunya Abu 'Amr, who witnessed Uhud and the campaigns after it. He was among the ten Ansar whom 'Umar sent to Kufa to teach the people, he built a house in Kufa, and he served as governor of Kufa under 'Ali bin Abi Talib. His mother was Khalidah bint Thabit and he was a half-brother of 'Abdullah bin Unays.

bio: A companion of Banu Sulaym who settled in Basra and led Banu Sulaym on the day of the Battle of the Camel, where he was killed in 36 AH before the main fighting. He took part in early conquests (including the campaign toward Kabul) and was known for his generosity, once giving 'Amr bin Ma'dikarib ten thousand dirhams plus a horse, sword and armor. Five of his hadiths are recorded in the Sahihayn and other collections.

bio: The entries identify Shuqran as the mawla of the Messenger of Allah, known by this laqab, his name said to be Salih. He was present at Badr but was not allotted a share of the booty (شهد شقران بدرا فلم يسهم له), and at the Prophet's burial he was the one who placed the qatifa (velvet cloth) beneath him in the grave. Originally enslaved by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, he came to the Prophet and was freed after Badr; his line of descendants ended in Medina during al-Rashid's reign.
